weather.reason: Alphabet's record one-day drop, then Intel and Amazon misses, broke the AI trade: Nasdaq-100 -2.0% on the week, chips -9% Friday, while defensives rose.

take.what_happened: Alphabet fell 12.6% Thursday, its worst day ever, on a search-ad miss and negative free cash flow; Intel (-24% on the week) and Amazon's $42.4B cash outflow sank chips Friday. The Fed held at 3.75-4.00%.
take.why_it_matters: Investors now demand AI profits, not just AI spending. Communication services fell 5.3% and tech 2.0% while health care, materials and utilities each rose 2-3%: a rotation, not a crash. The S&P 500 slipped only 0.57%.
take.what_to_watch: Apple and Palantir Monday, AMD Tuesday, Arm and Qualcomm Wednesday, the midterms Tuesday and October payrolls Friday (consensus +55K). A strong Apple print would steady mega-cap tech.

jargon.definition: Cash a company has left after paying operating costs and capital spending.
jargon.why_it_matters: Alphabet and Amazon went negative this week, and that is what stock prices punished.

jargon.definition: Money moving out of one group of stocks into another rather than leaving the market.
jargon.why_it_matters: Tech fell while health care and staples rose, so the S&P 500 barely moved.

jargon.definition: The average closing price over the last 200 trading days, a widely watched trend line.

jargon.definition: A Fed voter who votes against the majority decision.
jargon.why_it_matters: Two members wanted a hike, a sign the next move is more likely up than down.

jargon.definition: The date insiders may start selling shares after an IPO.
